title: Add KV cache hit/miss counters + initial miss-reason enum
author: Samir Qureshi
body:
## Summary
Adds core runtime counters for KV cache lookups (hit/miss) and an initial, stable-ish miss-reason enum. This is the first building block for prefix/KV cache telemetry so Platform/SRE can quantify cache effectiveness and correlate regressions with throughput/cost.

## Motivation
We have multiple signals for “cache seems worse” (cost up, prefill time up) but nothing objective that’s joinable to model/route/region context yet. This PR deliberately keeps the surface small: a single lookup counter (tagged by result + reason on miss) plus unit tests to lock down behavior.

This is intended to land before:
- gateway/context tag propagation (route/model/version/deployment_mode)
- sampling + rate-limits
- dashboards/alerts

## Metrics (initial)
Emitted from runtime KV cache lookup path (prefill stage):
- `redwood.runtime.kv_cache.lookup_total{result="hit"}`
- `redwood.runtime.kv_cache.lookup_total{result="miss", miss_reason="..."}`

Miss reasons (v0):
- `not_found`: key not present in cache (cold)
- `evicted`: key existed but was evicted before reuse
- `disabled`: cache disabled by policy/config for the request
- `capacity`: cache could not admit entry due to capacity constraints
- `unknown`: fallback bucket for unexpected states

Notes:
- We are intentionally *not* emitting high-cardinality labels here (no tenant/route/model). Those will be wired in a follow-up with allowlists + ingestion guards.
- Naming is aligned with our current runtime metric prefix, but final naming/cardinality policy is being reviewed; we can rename once the observability standards doc lands.

## Implementation details
- Adds `KvCacheLookupResult` (hit/miss) and `KvCacheMissReason` enum in runtime cache module.
- Increments counters once per lookup attempt.
- Ensures lookup accounting is not double-counted on early-return paths.
- Uses pre-allocated label handles to avoid per-request allocations.

## Tests
- Unit tests cover:
  - hit increments hit counter only
  - miss increments miss counter with expected miss_reason
  - disabled path increments miss/disabled
  - capacity rejection increments miss/capacity

## Perf note
Microbench on A100 (single worker, synthetic repeated prompts) indicates no measurable regression within noise at p95; worst-case overhead observed was ~0.2–0.4% in a tight loop benchmark when metrics are enabled at full rate. Sampling/rate-limiting will be added separately (ENG-4821/ENG-4825 follow-ups) to keep production overhead near-zero.

## Follow-ups
- Add standardized tags (model_id/version, route_id, deployment_mode, region) with strict allowlists (ENG-4823).
- Add sampling controls + local rate limits for high-volume paths.
- Add eviction/pressure and wasted-prefill signals once lookup accounting is stable.

## Checklist
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Bench run / perf spot-check
- [x] No prompt logging / privacy-safe
- [ ] Dashboards (separate PR)

Refs: ENG-4822, ENG-4821
commits: runtime/cache: introduce KvCacheMissReason enum and map from lookup outcomes
runtime: add unit tests for hit/miss + miss_reason accounting
docs(internal): add brief note on interpreting kv_cache.lookup_total
review_conversation: Omar El-Sayed (review): Please keep the miss_reason taxonomy small + stable; we can expand later but dashboards will depend on it. Also make sure the metric is incremented exactly once per lookup attempt (some early-return paths look suspicious).

Samir Qureshi (author): Agreed. Kept reasons to 5 buckets and added a comment that expansions require Telemetry sign-off. Also refactored lookup() to funnel all returns through a single accounting point; added a unit test to guard against double increments.

Nadia Rahman (review): Naming looks fine for now, but we should avoid baking in anything that conflicts with the observability standards doc. Can you add a TODO noting this will likely be renamed in the metrics reconciliation PR? Also, ensure we’re not adding any labels beyond result/miss_reason here.
Samir Qureshi (author): Added TODO + explicit note in the PR description. No additional labels in this PR; wiring of model/route context will happen after allowlists are implemented.
Marcus Reed (review): Perf: counters in the hot path worry me. Did you validate overhead with metrics enabled? Even a small regression at p99 could be painful.

Samir Qureshi (author): Ran the microbench in `runtime/bench/kv_cache_lookup_bench` with metrics on/off. Seeing 0.2–0.4% worst-case overhead in a tight loop; p95 in the synthetic workload is within noise. Added the numbers to the perf note and flagged follow-up for sampling/rate-limits.
Noah Patel (review): Minor: `unknown` should be a true last resort. Please make sure we don’t default to unknown when we actually know the state (e.g., disabled vs not_found).
Samir Qureshi (author): Fixed mapping to ensure disabled/capacity are preserved; unknown is only used if we hit an unexpected branch. Added an assertion in tests for disabled mapping.
Omar El-Sayed (review): LGTM after the single-accounting change + tests.
Nadia Rahman (review): Approved. Please tag follow-up PRs to keep the taxonomy consistent.
Marcus Reed (review): Approved with perf note; sampling follow-up is required before broad rollout.
release_notes: Internal: runtime now emits `redwood.runtime.kv_cache.lookup_total` counters for KV cache hit/miss with initial miss_reason breakdown. No customer-facing changes yet; tagging/sampling/dashboards to follow.
